<algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        const cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                          \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Thread block shape. x is the fastest-varying index (contiguous in memory),\n// so it is mapped to the warp lanes for coalesced accesses.\nconstexpr unsigned int BLOCK_X = 32;\nconstexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Y = 4;\nconstexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Z = 4;\n\n// 3D index calculation\n__host__ __device__ inline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Compute Laplacian with clamped boundary conditions\n__device__ __forceinline__ double computeLaplacian(const double* __restrict__ c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                                   const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                                                   const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z) {\n    const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n    const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n\n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] -\n                        2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] -\n                        2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (c[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)] -\n                        2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dz * dz);\n\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Chemical potential kernel: one thread per cell (grid-stride over y/z for large grids)\n__global__ void computeChemicalPotentialKernel(const double* __restrict__ c, double* __restrict__ mu,\n                                               const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                               const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                                               const double gamma, const double e_AA, const double e_BB, const double e_AB) {\n    const size_t x = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * BLOCK_X + threadIdx.x;\n    if (x >= nx) return;\n    const size_t yStride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.y) * BLOCK_Y;\n    const size_t zStride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.z) * BLOCK_Z;\n\n    for (size_t z = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.z) * BLOCK_Z + threadIdx.z; z < nz; z += zStride) {\n        for (size_t y = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * BLOCK_Y + threadIdx.y; y < ny; y += yStride) {\n            const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n            const double cv = c[idx];\n\n            mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n                    + 3.0 * {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793025692085,"sessionID":"ses_e87595c6dffeGohy0dHD2W5vfM","part":{"id":"prt_178a8b296001o90cANwDo7D16z","messageID":"msg_178a8ac99001wvyLtXIh4tFPqV","sessionID":"ses_e87595c6dffeGohy0dHD2W5vfM","type":"reasoning","text":"The reference build's FMA-contraction hash matches exactly with the GPU's strict `--fmad=false` output, meaning the GPU's non-FMA mode aligns with strict IEEE semantics, while the reference's default behavior actually depends on FMA contraction from its own compiler flags. This raises the question of which version should count as the true \"equivalent semantics\" baseline — the original as compiled by its own CMake settings, or the strict IEEE path.\n\nTrying to replicate the exact contraction pattern GCC uses to match it bit-for-bit seems impractical, and nvcc's default FMA mode didn't match either. I decide the cleanest approach is to standardize on `--fmad=false` for the CUDA build, documenting that this diverges in the last bit from the native `-march=native` reference, and now I want to check how this flag affects performance at the larger problem size.\n\nI need a bigger benchmark, maybe a 256^3 grid run for 100 iterations, comparing fmad true vs false timing, then updating CMakeLists to add the `--fmad=false` flag permanently. I also note the tiny-grid timing shows \"inf\" just like the original build, confirming consistent behavior. I should also test edge cases: non-cubic grids, nx=1, and grids large enough to exceed the 65535 limit in the y-dimension of the CUDA grid, which would trigger the grid-stride loop path — something like 2×300000×1 cells with 2 iterations would be a good stress test against the CPU reference.\n\n","time":{"start":1793025684118,"end":1793025691989},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793025692086,"sessionID":"ses_e87595c6dffeGohy0dHD2W5vfM","part":{"id":"prt_178a8d158001FvRXhfKCw7vhBF","messageID":"msg_178a8ac99001wvyLtXIh4tFPqV","sessionID":"ses_e87595c6dffeGohy0dHD2W5vfM","type":"text","text":"This settles it. The CPU reference built with `-march=native` (GCC's default `-ffp-contract=fast`) uses FMA, and it is not the same as strict IEEE evaluation. The GPU build with `--fmad=false` reproduces the strict, non-FMA CPU results bit-for-bit (`50c807064ce3c1ed`, `ea1403457896b673`, `d49bfc3f9a5eefeb`). I'll make `--fmad=false` the permanent CUDA setting, since it's deterministic and matches the original's unfused arithmetic. I'll then check performance and the edge cases, including a y-dimension large enough to exercise the grid-stride loop.","time":{"start":1793025691992,"end":1793025692011}}}
